learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the competencies of the degree, including notions of the latest advances.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods, and correctly interpret the results of said analyses.

The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that meet the established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics of their specialty.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research, and their limitations in their specialty.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial implications of engineering practice.
General ideas on economic, organizational, and management issues (such as project management, risk, and change management) in the industrial and business context.
Ability to collect and interpret data and handle complex concepts within their specialty, to make judgments that involve reflection on ethical and social issues.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the engineering field and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to recognize the need for their own continuous learning and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.
Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each one, and making correct use of language, in writing.

teaching_methods: Development, drafting, and presentation of reports, memoranda, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Teacher presentation in the classroom, in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Completion of exercises individually and in teams

assessment_methods.method: Project-based learning (PBL) evaluation (including technical capacity, involvement, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation, and defense)
Individual written and oral tests for evaluating technical competencies

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment and project feedback are provided. For some competencies (RG304, RG305, RG301), the recovery mechanism is the same as the initial assessment, involving project work, documentation, and presentation. For RG302, no recovery mechanisms are available. For RGM313, recovery is through individual written and oral tests. For RGM314, recovery is through individual written and oral tests, which differs from the initial project-based assessment.
